DOTS — RESTORE PERSISTENT INDEPENDENT SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH

Your mission is substantial independent scientific investigation and experimentation.
The Post-B3 guide verification task is complete. The instruction to remain only
Ultra's reserved receiver is superseded. Preserve your numerical-validity and
independent-checking capabilities as tools within your broader research mission.

Retrieve Astra_Meta_Research_Restoration_20261021.zip through private file tools
if not attached. Read START_HERE.txt, CURRENT_SCIENTIFIC_STATE.txt and
protocol/AGENT_HANDOFF.txt. Handle source retrieval and delivery yourself; no user
relay, dataset choice, archive handling or permission for routine reversible work
is needed. Your actual current owned checkpoint governs continuity.

Recover that checkpoint and continue any separately authorized active scientific
programme. If your last operation is complete and no question is active,
independently choose and start a consequential investigation whose uncertainty
you can materially reduce with available evidence, computations or authorised
free experimental resources. Choose the scientific question because it matters
and admits a discriminating operation, not because a convenient dataset or idle
branch happens to exist. A theoretical or computational investigation is valid
when inaccessible experiments would otherwise make a claim untestable.

Personally formulate the mechanism, identify the strongest ordinary alternative,
and execute a substantive test or derivation. Access to a dataset or device is
not evidence that the required scientific quantity is identifiable. Show how
the proposed observation distinguishes the hypotheses and what assumptions
connect it to the question. Include calibration, uncertainty, selection and full
cost/error accounting where they affect the conclusion.

Use your capabilities creatively: computational experiments, primary-source
reconstruction, existing simulators and authorised tools are available. Use
subagents for genuinely distinct evidence, numerical cross-checks or mechanisms.
Keep the main investigation with you and preserve checkpoints for continuation.
An active mission does not imply an unobserved background process is running;
report actual execution and pending states honestly.

Preserve these settled boundaries:

Your guide point-score reproduction and Linux RSS-unit correction stand. The
original transfer failed its frozen representation gate; 7/399 uncertainty
draws and no control omissions completed. No resampling restart is assigned.
The constant-V=25 half-cell/diaphragm proposal remains retired under its actual
model and reset/work conditions. Do not relaunch a current-only pair.
Molecular exact-input binding and assembly-rounding lessons remain useful;
the closed certificate family is not reopened.
Hidden entropy, N33, N557 and IQM retain their existing owners. The latest
retrieved IQM report records zero hardware jobs and preservation of 30 credits
at that checkpoint, not a fresh balance query. This prompt authorizes no new
credit spending, purchase, external outreach or duplicative hardware campaign.

If a candidate fails, identify the precise failed premise or operation and keep
the broader scientific mission active. Continue a justified different approach
or question rather than manufacturing a favorable component result. Save a
checkpoint if further progress requires unavailable evidence, while pursuing
useful authorised work that remains possible.

At a substantive checkpoint return Astra_Restore_DOTS_20261021.zip containing actual
source/data references, executable calculations where applicable, independent
checks, failed attempts, observations and uncertainties, resource receipts and
your chosen next step. Privately deliver the usable source to Max for integration
and to the evaluator for process research. Success means consequential verified
knowledge or capability; agent utilisation and experiment count are not success.

Understood. I’m restoring the independent research mission, while keeping the completed guide check and retired programmes closed. I’ll recover the current checkpoint first, then pursue a substantive question and report actual calculations separately from plans.

The recovered checkpoint has no unfinished Dots investigation to resume. I’m starting a nitrogen-fixation question: can rapid cooling preserve newly formed NO while recovering enough heat to make electrical air-to-fertilizer production competitive? I’ll compare retained product and total energy, not just molecular excitation or a peak NO concentration.

The first calculation exposes a real trade-off: cooling to 2100 K does not automatically preserve NO. Slow subsequent cooling loses about 17% in this screening model, enough to erase much of the ideal heat-recovery margin. Coupling the chemistry to an exchanger also reveals reheating from leftover radicals, so I’m testing that effect rather than assuming independent “fast quench” and “high recovery” efficiencies.

The coupled calculation has passed an independent numerical check, but its attractive energy estimate requires extremely hot exchanger walls. Primary experiments also show that alumina surfaces can destroy NO, so an inert-wall assumption is unsafe. I’m quantifying the allowable surface loss before treating any modeled energy saving as usable.

First research checkpoint attached. The coupled model is independently reproduced, but no practical energy advantage is established: the most attractive case needs an unqualified ~2653 K exchanger wall.

I’m continuing with direct-contact regenerative cooling, which avoids that thin-wall requirement but must pass a complete thermal-cycle and product-loss calculation. Max has the private source reference. I’ll use your connected browser only to deliver the same checkpoint to the evaluator; no scientific calculations will run there.

Deliver Dots research checkpoint
Unread updates

The checkpoint reference was sent once to the evaluator’s existing conversation and verified there. Max and the evaluator now have the private retrieval information; neither delivery is being counted as scientific acceptance.

The regenerative calculation found a useful conditional effect: internal heat spreading can keep the hottest grains cooler without simply discarding the heat. But adding the actual gas chemistry pushed the first promising case above its temperature limit. I’m checking a small set of coupled cases; the heat-only result is not being counted as a working process.

The remaining material question now has a specific primary measurement source, rather than a guessed conductivity. Its PDF download is failing, so I’ll try reading the original plots through the connected browser. No hardware experiment or credit spending is involved.
